content: 1. In 2009, a study published in volume 50, issue 1, pages 77-83, explored the knowledge and acceptability of alternative HIV prevention biomedical products among men who have sex with men (MSM) who engage in barebacking practices. 2. Nodin N, Carballo-Dieguez A, Ventuneac AM, Balan IC, and Remien R conducted research in 2008, published in AIDS Care (volume 20, issue 1, pages 106-115), examining the awareness and acceptance of alternative HIV prevention methods among MSM who engage in unprotected sexual practices. 3. Their study, published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2011 (volume 22, issue 5, pages 256-262), identified barriers and facilitators to PrEP uptake among at-risk populations in Peru. 4. Van Griensven F, Thienkrua W, Sukwicha W, and others conducted a study on sexual frequency and planning among MSM in Bangkok, Thailand. 5. Poynten IM, Jin F, Prestage GP, Kaldor JM, Imrie J, and Grulich AE examined attitudes toward new HIV biomedical prevention technologies among a cohort of HIV-negative gay men in Sydney, Australia. Their research was published in HIV Medicine in 2010 (volume 11, issue 4, pages 282-288). 6. Liu A, Lubensky D, Koester K, and colleagues explored barriers and facilitators to the use of prevention pills in the iPrEx study. Their work, which captured the experiences of MSM participants in the United States, was published in the Journal of the International Association of Physicians in AIDS Care in 2010 (volume 9, issue 4, pages 261-262). 7. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, GA, USA, contributed to the body of knowledge on HIV prevention strategies and their implementation.
